s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal symptoms with weight loss and bowel obstruction
salient_findings: Worsening abdominal distention and 60-lb unintentional weight loss over 1 year
Small-bowel obstruction with focal wall thickening and mesenteric adenopathy
Multiple dilated loops of small bowel with air-fluid levels
Multiple small-bowel ulcers and atrophic duodenum
Perforated ulcer in the terminal ileum
key_facts: 55-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and opioid use disorder
Presented with worsening abdominal distention and unintentional weight loss
Increasing difficulty with bowel movements
Denied melena, nausea, vomiting, fevers, flank pain, dysphagia, or odynophagia
No history of abdominal surgery
Abdominal CT with contrast showed small-bowel obstruction
Colonoscopy revealed two polyps with non-specific chronic inflammation
Video capsule endoscopy demonstrated erythematous gastritis and multiple small-bowel ulcers
Double-balloon enteroscopy identified multiple jejunal strictures
Exploratory laparotomy revealed a perforated ulcer in the terminal ileum
Biopsies around the perforation showed ulcerated mucosa with non-specific chronic inflammation
Ileoscopy showed scalloped mucosa with blunted villi throughout the ileum
Histologic examination revealed extensive lymphocytic infiltrates with epitheliotropism

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal symptoms, weight loss, bowel obstruction, and small-bowel ulcers

shortlist.label: Intestinal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive lymphocytic infiltrates with epitheliotropism and suspicion for lymphoma

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammation and ulceration in the colon and small bowel

shortlist.label: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Small-bowel ulcers, strictures, and lymphocytic infiltrates

shortlist.label: NSAID-induced enteropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of chronic abdominal symptoms and potential NSAID use

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening abdominal distention, unintentional weight loss, and increasing difficulty with bowel movements, along with findings of small-bowel obstruction, multiple jejunal strictures, and perforated ulcer in the terminal ileum, are consistent with Crohn's disease. The presence of non-specific chronic inflammation, erythematous gastritis, and multiple small-bowel ulcers also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intestinal lymphoma
rejected.why: While histologic examination revealed extensive lymphocytic infiltrates, there were no definitive atypical morphological features to support a diagnosis of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings are more consistent with small-bowel involvement, which is less typical of ulcerative colitis.

rejected.label: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of celiac disease or other enteropathy to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: NSAID-induced enteropathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of NSAID use in the patient's history, making this diagnosis less likely.
